html:
SMTO-UI-0006 — This update belongs to a different conversation or task

GUID: 5fe8b1f7-9d99-443b-8b4d-1207b72f7d4a
Slug: ui-state-stale
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • You moved to another conversation or task while something was still loading, so SMTO didn't apply it to the page you're on now. The command may still have done its work on the task it started from.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Refresh the browser page and open the conversation or task you meant to work on from the conversation list. The page dropped this update because a different conversation or task was showing when it arrived.
  2. Before running the command again, look at that task's status and latest messages to see whether the command already took effect (for example, a stopped task shows as stopped). The command may have finished on the server even though this page didn't show the result.
  3. If it didn't take effect, stay on that conversation and run the command again without switching views until it finishes. Switching conversations while a command runs is the usual reason its result no longer matches the page.

What success looks like

  • The command's result or the live output appears in the conversation you have open, with no new error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating the command until you've confirmed it hasn't already run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser dropped a command result or live stream update because its conversation, run or operation ID no longer matches the view captured when it started, or the stream event ID was invalid.

What this means

  • A client action or stream record no longer matches captured conversation/run/operation scope, or a stream event identity is invalid. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A client action or stream record no longer matches captured conversation/run/operation scope, or a stream event identity is invalid.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare captured identities, navigation and stream cursor validity with the active view.

How to fix it

  • Compare the client_action or stream record's conversation_id/request_id/operation_id with the current view (command_actions.js, command_palette.js, mobile/lazy/commands.js, shell_live_stream.js, model_output_viewer.js). Reload the intended conversation and inspect the saved run state before resubmitting; never replay the stale identifier.
  • Refresh the intended run and discard stale controls; reconcile saved state before applying the action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Current controls and updates refer to the intended run and valid cursor sequence.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
